newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks tumble 3.33 percent by lunch.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks tumble 3.33 percent by lunch.

text.p: Thai stocks continued to fall on Wednesday, dropping another 3.33 percent in thin dealings by the lunch break as economic worries led investors to sell, traders said.

The SET Index, which opened at a 5-1/2 year low of 643.28, had lost a further 21.45 points by the recess to 621.83. The SET 50 lost 1.84 points or 3.89 percent to 45.51. Turnover was a modest 1.65 million baht.
Lower economic growth prospects, loan quality concerns and expectations of further poor first quarter earnings results combined to undermine sentiment, analysts said.

"Investors are concerned about the loan portfolio quality. People are worried the non-performing loan figures banks and finance companies must declare at the end of the second quarter will be very bad," said Somchai Trairattanapirom, vice-president at Sitca Investment and Securities.
Uncertanties surrounding a number of mergers in the finance sector also contributed to weaker sentiment in the finance sector which lost 4.26 percent.
Lower economic growth prospects and reduced expectations of a strong recovery also undermined sentiment and fuelled sales of bank, energy and consumer stocks, analysts said.
Many private forecasters expect the Thai economy to grow by about five percent in 1997, its lowest level in a decade.
Property stocks were down 5.16 percent, hit by concerns surrounding liquidity in the sector, which faces high financing costs and declining market prices this year, analysts said.
Communications stocks fell 4.56 percent on fears increased competition in the mobile phone sector could hit operators' profits and lower economic growth may reduce fixed-line demand.
Bangkok Bank shed six baht to 166, Siam Cement lost 24 to 129, and PTTEP was off 22 to 290.
